Performance

Vektor Flow 0.4.7 publishes local, same-host measurements rather than a cross-platform ranking. Times are raw-kernel mean ± sample SD in milliseconds. Each ratio is VKF time divided by the named peer, so below 1× is faster.

Every populated native cell uses 5 warmups followed by 10 measured runs. An em dash (—) means that exact release, workload, platform, browser, or comparison was not measured. It is not a zero and it does not inherit a result from an older release.

Native language comparison

The Windows x64 and Linux x64 rows compare the same VKF workload with C++, Rust, and Zig on the same local host. Only VKF has an absolute time; the peer columns are VKF divided by that peer. This release does not publish a macOS compiler or macOS benchmark.

Methodology and reproduction · Windows JSON receipt · Linux JSON receipt

Download the exact compilers used for these measurements: Windows x64 compiler (SHA-256 f2a39904a56b4a6956aed475b5946399f40431230add0adbb94f54601b7e9897) and Linux x64 compiler (SHA-256 c9bc1068779c527d663a8254e66154463b30f6370aedec135d92f710034bdf38). The general installers contain a different compiler executable; these native timings do not describe those installers.

Browser WebAssembly versus native

Firefox runs version-matched VKF, C++, Rust, and Zig WebAssembly on the same Windows x64 host. The browser values are batched warm kernel means per operation. The VKF source is also timed as a raw native kernel on that host, so the final column compares Firefox WASM with native VKF. Chrome and Safari were not run for this release.
